walkthroughs.body_html:
Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates.

They float on the semi-molten mantle and move at roughly the speed your fingernails grow — a few centimetres per year.

Constructive: plates pull apart (Mid-Atlantic Ridge — Iceland).

Destructive: oceanic plate subducts under continental (Pacific Ring of Fire — Japan).

Conservative: plates slide past (San Andreas Fault — California).

Collisional: two continental plates collide (Himalayas).

When plates lock, stress builds. The sudden release sends shock waves outwards from the focus underground.

The point directly above on the surface is the epicentre — where shaking is usually strongest.

mcqs.q: At which boundary do plates pull APART?
options: Constructive
Destructive
Conservative
Collisional

mcqs.q: What is the point on the SURFACE directly above an earthquake called?
options: Focus
Epicentre
Hypocentre
Margin
Earthquakes are caused by magma rising up to the surface.
The sudden release of built-up stress along faults at plate boundaries as rocks slip past each other, generating seismic waves.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the focus and epicentre of an earthquake?
options: The focus and epicentre are the same point.
The focus (hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes of similar magnitude cause different amounts of damage?
options: Bigger magnitude always means more deaths.
Damage depends on depth, distance from population, building quality, ground type (liquefaction risk), time of day, and emergency preparedness — not just magnitude.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
